newsitem.title: USA: CBOT SOYBEANS END SHARPLY LOWER ON WEATHER, FCC.
newsitem.headline: CBOT SOYBEANS END SHARPLY LOWER ON WEATHER, FCC.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended sharply lower on Thursday as funds sold amid bearishly construed weather and crop production forecasts, traders said.

"We're in the critical time frame for soybeans," said Don Roose, president of U.S. Commodities. "We either make or break them in August. There's been no irreversable damage done to soybeans. If we get the (rain) there's a big probability that we will have above trend-line yields in soybeans."
Soybeans ended 23-1/2 to 12 cents per bushel lower with November down 21-1/2 at $6.28-1/2 and August off 23-1/2 at $7.45-1/2.
Weather Services Corp meteorologist Joel Burgio said weekend storms would likely bring 0.25 to 0.75 inch of rain to the U.S. Midwest with 40 to 50 percent coverage.

But there was a slight chance that a second system brewing in the U.S. South would bring heavier precipitation, he said. Traders said other meteorologists also suggested more rains were possible in some dry areas on the central Corn Belt.

Farmers Commodities Corp's U.S. soybean crop production estimate, released on Wednesday, was also deemed bearish. FCC put soybean output at 2.73 billion bushels. That figure was above USDA's July outlook for 2.69 billion bushels.

The FCC number represented a record large soybean crop and was above USDA's July outlook for 2.69 billion. It was also the highest trade estimate in a Reuter survey of analysts released on Thursday. That survey produced an average crop production estimate of 2.68 billion bushels.
USDA will release its August crop production estimate on Tuesday at 0730 CDT/1230 GMT.

Export sales data was deemed supportive but bearish weather and crop forecasts quickly overshadowed the export news. USDA Thursday said U.S. net export sales of old crop and new crop soybeans were at 405,400 tonnes and 295,600 tonnes, respectively. The old crop number was sharply above expectations and the new crop number was at the high end of expectations.

On the day, funds sold at least 12 million bushels of soybeans. Refco Inc sold 3.5 million November and one million September while Lind-Waldock and Cargill Investor Services each sold three million November.
Rand Financial bear spread two million bushels November/August at $1.23 to $1.25, premium August. Continental Grain, Merrill Lynch and Tenco Inc were also said to be bear spreaders.
In options, Smith Barney bought 600 November $6.50 calls at 26-1/2 to 27 cents and bought 200 November $5.25 puts at 1-3/4 cents.
Volatility in the November was pegged at 27-1/2 percent, up slightly from Wednesday's 27 percent.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 44,000 contracts, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 45,113.
